name: typethatbook-functions
description: Cloud Functions for TypeThatBook practice mode (one export: generatePractice), plus the dev-only harness suite.
//engines: Node 18 was decommissioned for Cloud Functions deploys, so the previous pin
would have failed at the worst possible moment: the first time anyone tried
to deploy, probably while debugging something else.
⚠⚠ ROUND 81: THIS SAID 22 AND THE DEPLOYED FUNCTION IS ON 24. Round 80
fixed the UTC-day bug in functions/index.js, Jake redeployed it through the
Cloud Run console, and took the Node 20 deprecation prompt to Node 24 while he
was there. So this field has now disagreed with the live runtime TWICE over,
in both directions: it said 22 while the function ran on 20, and then kept
saying 22 after the function moved to 24. It was never once the truth.
⚠ THE REASON IT DRIFTS IS THE REASON NOTHING CAUGHT IT: deploys here are
console clicks, not `firebase deploy`, so nothing ever READS this field. It is
documentation that looks like configuration, which is the worst kind — and
firebase.json has no `functions` block at all, so a CLI deploy could not run
from this repo today even if someone had one.
⚠⚠ IT IS STILL WORTH KEEPING ACCURATE, AND HERE IS THE CONCRETE COST OF
NOT: the day anyone DOES wire up a CLI deploy, this field is what picks the
runtime, and a stale 22 would silently DOWNGRADE a function running on 24.
That failure arrives as a deploy that appears to succeed. functions/index.js's
own header says to treat that file as the record of what is running; this
field is part of the same record and is held to the same standard.
//main: The Cloud Function source moved to functions/index.js in the Round 17 tidy,
so it stops sitting next to index.html looking like the site's entry point.
It is still not deployable from this repo — that needs `firebase deploy`.
//dependencies: PRODUCTION ONLY. Everything listed here is uploaded and installed on every
Cloud Functions deploy, and is paid for in cold-start time. If a package is
only imported by a *-test.mjs or *-harness.mjs file, it belongs below.
//devDependencies: ⚠️ THESE WERE MISSING, AND TWO ROUNDS OF HANDOFF DISAGREED ABOUT WHETHER
THEY WERE. Round 7 reported that the harnesses need packages package.json
does not declare. Round 8 called that False and wrote 'jsdom, acorn,
acorn-walk and jszip are all declared' into both the README and the handoff
— in the same section that added the invariant 'verify your own complaints
before writing them down'. They were not declared. Round 8's container
happened to have them installed from an earlier session, the suite ran, and
a working test run was read as proof of a declaration nobody opened the file
to check.
Consequence, until now: `git clone && npm install && node run-all-tests.mjs`
failed on a fresh machine with seven ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND errors, and the
documented remedy was to install them by hand — which then wrote them into
`dependencies`, where they would ride along to the next functions deploy.
devDependencies is the correct home: `firebase deploy` installs production
dependencies only, so nothing here reaches the deployed function.
jsdom      — the ten DOM harnesses (about-render, card-markup, credits, ...)
acorn      — undefined-calls-test.mjs parses every shipped file
acorn-walk — same
jszip      — the EPUB corpus harnesses (--with-epubs)
@xmldom/xmldom — tests/cover-harness.mjs, and ONLY that harness. It was the
one package the old install line named that package.json did not
declare, which is why cover-harness.mjs is the one harness in
tests/ that a fresh clone could not run. Declared now. It is
still not registered in run-all-tests.mjs — see tests/README.md.
//type: ⚠️ DO NOT ADD "type": "module" HERE TO SILENCE THE NODE WARNING.
Every harness run prints MODULE_TYPELESS_PACKAGE_JSON about daylog.js and
suggests exactly that fix. It would break the Cloud Function:
functions/index.js is CommonJS — `const { onCall } = require(...)` — and is
what `main` points at. "type": "module" makes .js mean ESM package-wide,
so the next `firebase deploy` fails on a require() the warning never
mentioned. The harnesses are .mjs and already unambiguous; the warning is
about daylog.js, which the browser loads as a module via a <script
type=module> tag and which Node only sees at all because the tests import
it. It is noise, it costs a few milliseconds, and the cure is worse.
If it ever becomes worth removing: rename functions/index.js to .cjs and
repoint `main`, in a round that can watch a deploy.
//scripts: `npm test` exists so the suite has one obvious entry point. run-all-tests.mjs
skips the EPUB corpus harnesses unless you pass --with-epubs, because those
need the library/ folder and take minutes rather than seconds.
Paths are repo-root relative — package.json is the only file at the root that
knows where the suite lives, which is the point of putting it here.
⚠️ THIS ARRAY AND THE EMULATOR NOTE BELOW USED TO BE TWO SEPARATE
"//scripts" KEYS, AND JSON DOES NOT ALLOW THAT — last one wins. Everything
above this line was silently discarded by every parser that read the file,
which is a comment that had been deleted for as long as anyone had been
reading it. Merged into one array in Round 25. ⚠️ If you add another note,
add it HERE; do not open a second key.
test:rules NEEDS THE FIREBASE EMULATOR — a JVM and a one-time jar download
from storage.googleapis.com. It is deliberately NOT part of `npm test`,
because a fresh clone cannot be assumed to have java and a suite that fails
on a missing JVM teaches people to ignore it.
It is here because firestore.rules is the ONE file Jake cannot test from a
browser (the Rules editor is console-only), which makes it the file that most
needs executing. firestore-rules.test.mjs carried an 'I COULD NOT RUN THIS'
header for four rounds; it was false, and Round 20 designed a fix the
deployed rules reject because nobody spent the nine seconds. HANDOFF 0.-5.A.
First run installs the emulator deps: npm run test:rules:setup
demo-ttb is a fake project id. Nothing here touches production.
TWO SEPARATE mocha INVOCATIONS, ON PURPOSE. Both harnesses declare root-level
hooks that seed and clear the emulator; in ONE mocha process those hooks
interleave and each file wipes the other seed, which surfaces as five
Null value error denials that look exactly like broken rules. Do not merge
these back into one mocha call to save three seconds.

scripts.test:rules: firebase emulators:exec --only firestore --project demo-ttb "mocha tests/rules-probe.test.mjs --timeout 20000 && mocha tests/firestore-rules.test.mjs --timeout 20000"
